newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Ex-BTA head invited to head Expo '98 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ex-BTA head invited to head Expo '98 - paper.

text.p: A former president of Banco Totta e Acores, Alipio Dias, was invited by Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres to become the chief organiser of the Expo 1998 World Fair in Lisbon, Diario de Noticias newspaper reported.
The reply of Dias, who was replaced as head of Totta by Luis Champalimaud last week, was not known, the paper said.
Dias and Guterres were not immediately available to confirm the report.

Antonio Cardoso e Cunha quit as chief organiser of Expo 1998 on Tuesday, saying he could not maintain a climate of "political neutrality" in the project and that he lacked adequate management conditions.

Press reports said government officials were angry when Cardoso e Cunha told them this month that Expo 1998 would cost the government more than initial estimates of 200 billion escudos ($1.2 billion).
Portuguese media said the government would have to appoint a well-qualified successor to Cardoso e Cunha as soon as possible to restore confidence in the organisation of the event.
